messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-runtime kvcache memory > 92% on shard pool-g-7c (prefetcher spike). Auto-scaling attempted, 2x queue latency increase. Incident ticket: INC-2026-1837.
maya: seeing a series of long prompts from a single API key, looks like prefix amplification. Sessions spiking kv_size per req.
sachin: thumbs. Can you dump top keys?
daria: attaching quick tail logs: ```
[2026-03-15T12:04:11Z] req_id=ab12 kv_alloc=8.1GB ctx_len=96k tokens_in=24000 prefetch_hits=0
[2026-03-15T12:04:12Z] req_id=ab13 kv_alloc=7.9GB ctx_len=88k tokens_in=22000
```
leo: that's huge. Those ctx_len numbers match longform ingestion from partner-prod. Might be streaming + continuous batching touching the same session with repeated prefix sends.
maya: hypothesis: prefetcher + continuous batching + large prefix replaying into shared kvcache leads to exponential kv entries (prefix copied per batch).
sachin: can we flip prefetcher to conservative mode on hosted runtime 7c? config flag is `kvcache.prefetch.mode=conservative` (prod rollout path).
daria: I've prepared a hotpatch: disable aggressive prefix replication and cap batch_window to 80 tokens for pool-g. Command: ```./deploy-control set pool=pool-g kvcache.prefetch.mode=conservative && ./deploy-control set pool=pool-g batch.max_window=80``` Planning to apply to one node first.
maya: please apply to all nodes in pool-g but in staggered fashion. Use 30s wait between nodes.
leo: also recommend immediate eviction policy change: `kvcache.eviction.bias=recent` to avoid old big prefixes sticking around.
sachin: applying to node pool-g-7c-01 now. Patch in canary...
incident-bot: deploy started (INC-2026-1837). Node pool-g-7c-01 -> success.
maya: monitoring memory. Latency dip looks better on canary.
sachin: rolling to pool-g-7c-02 and pool-g-7c-03...
support-sam: FYI CS flagged three customer sessions with 500 errors. IDs: cst-889, cst-890, cst-894. Any ETA to restore?
daria: customers will be back once nodes stabilize post-eviction. I'm seeing kvcache usage fall 40% after canary.
maya: good. Patch rolling complete. Observability: tokens/sec throughput stable, queue latency down to baseline.
leo: temporary mitigation notes: disabled aggressive prefetch, capped batch window, changed eviction bias. Need follow-ups: adjust continuous batching heuristics to avoid per-session kv duplication.
incident-bot: NOTE: Automatic fallback to smaller model variants observed twice during spike to maintain SLA for premium customers.
sachin: opened follow-up task INF-1259 to instrument per-prefix reference counting and to add a guard on prefix replication.
maya: created customer comms draft for impacted customers. @support-sam please review and send.
support-sam: will ping legal and send out targeted note to the 3 affected accounts within 30 minutes.
leo: perf cliff root cause summary: streaming + client-side re-sends of long prefix + continuous batching combined with prefetch aggressive replication created multiplicative kv entries per batch. Under high cardinality prefixes this yields OOM.
daria: mitigation checklist attached to INC-2026-1837: 1) apply conservative prefetch 2) cap batch_window 3) eviction bias change 4) start draining large stale keys 5) roll monitoring alert thresholds to detect prefix amplification.
maya: adding postmortem owners: sachin (runtime fix), daria (observability + alerts), leo (customer comms + risk gating for model fallbacks).
onchalant-reaction: :thumbsup:  
oncall-sre: taking handoff for midnight watch. Will keep an eye on pool-g and run a sweep job to evict keys > 1GB per-session.
maya: handing off live: handoff notes -> patch applied, memory trending down, watchlist keys pinned: cst-889 session ids; avoid restart.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. I'll escalate to infra if memory flares > 85% again.
sachin: one action item: throttle repeated prefix writes at the front-end ingress: INF-1260. We'll implement a short-term rate cap per-session to avoid immediate re-amplification.
daria: logging added: `prefetch.debug.prefix_counts` instrumented. We'll add a dashboard widget.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1837 status: mitigation applied, monitoring in watch, handoff to oncall-sre.
maya: closing notes: temporary patch reduced risk; root fix will require kvcache reference counting + batching heuristics change. Expect a scheduled maintenance window next week for runtime update.
support-sam: customer comms sent. No escalations so far.
oncall-sre: will post a short incident summary in #incidents-ops by EOD and link postmortem when ready.
maya: thanks everyone, excellent triage.
